page: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, with a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are included in this configuration, though it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation also demonstrate strong performance. Multi-core execution, database operations, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 38.03 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads and large-block writes remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F8ams_v6 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for deployments relying on external premium storage. This server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, text processing, and light language model inference.
